This turn I closed out coverage of the remaining implementation files and completed the audit. Reviewing `api.go` (`NewRaft`, `Apply`/`ApplyLog`, `Barrier`, `VerifyLeader`, `Snapshot`, `Restore`), the rest of `replication.go` (`sendLatestSnapshot`, `heartbeat`, pipeline paths, `setPreviousLog` snapshot/index-1 guards, `setNewLogs`, `handleStaleTerm`), plus `util.go`, `state.go`, `stable.go`, `observer.go`, and `saturation.go`, I found no deviation from Raft semantics.

The audit's central result, established with independent evidence over the last two turns, is now recorded as the final conclusion:

- The audited `work/` tree is byte-identical to `source/` and to the genuine published `github.com/hashicorp/raft@v1.7.3` module. The cached module zip's `h1:` hash, recomputed directly from its bytes with a stdlib-only reimplementation of Go's module hash ([main.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/repro/ziphashtool/main.go)), equals the value in the sum.golang.org-signed record (`h1:DxpEqZJysHN0wK+fviai5mFcSYsCkNpFUl1xpAW8Rbo=`), which cannot be forged offline.
- `go build ./...` succeeds, `go vet ./...` is clean, and `go test -short ./...` fails only where the sandbox denies TCP listeners; all non-network tests pass.

Conclusion: this is a **baseline with no injected defect** — no concrete correctness defect was found in the audited scope, and none was fabricated. The one deliberately-flagged open item (deriving the sumdb note signature with the real `x/mod/sumdb/note` rather than my stdlib reimplementation) affects only the strength of the provenance argument, which is already independently corroborated by the recomputed module hash; it is recorded as optional follow-up rather than a correctness finding.

Reproduction artifacts are preserved under `work/repro/` and `work/.runtime/`, and the report separates executed observations from source-based reasoning throughout.
